questions.q: Describe the image formed by a plane mirror, and distinguish between concave and convex mirrors.

answer.text: A flat, or plane, mirror forms an image that is virtual and erect, the same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and laterally inverted, meaning the left and right sides are exchanged.

Its reflecting surface curves inward and converges light. It can form real or virtual, magnified images and is used in shaving and dentists' mirrors, torch and headlight reflectors, and solar cookers.
Its surface curves outward and diverges light. It always forms a small, virtual, erect image and gives a wide field of view, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles.

questions.q: What is white light made of, and how can this be demonstrated?
answer: Sunlight, or white light, is not a single colour but a mixture of seven colours.

answer.text: These are violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red, remembered by the word VIBGYOR.

When white light passes through a glass prism, it splits into these seven colours, a process called dispersion. A rainbow forms in the same way when sunlight passes through tiny water droplets in the sky.
The reverse can also be shown: a disc painted with the seven colours, known as Newton's disc, appears white when spun rapidly, because the colours combine again to give white light.
